1.pericope_label: The LORD’s hand is not shortened; your iniquities have separated
debates: Whether the chapter is spoken by God or by the prophet
What the omission of idolatry from the list of sins implies
Whether the noun should read the face or his face
outliers: Clarke holds the divine speech closed with the previous chapter, against a scholar he cites who reads the pronoun as making God the speaker here
themes: Delay in deliverance traced to the hearers rather than to God
Sin described as a wall rather than a distance
A chapter praised for the exactness of its construction
An old indictment repeated word for word

4.pericope_label: They hatch cockatrice eggs and weave the spider’s web
debates: Whether the opening clause is about public testimony or about legal process
Whether the images describe false doctrine or violent scheming
What the crushing of the egg represents
outliers: Gill reads the whole passage of false teaching where the others read it of injustice and violence
themes: Justice failing at the point where it is pleaded
Schemes potent for harm and useless for good
A covering that cannot in fact cover
Conduct pictured as a road walked in haste

7.pericope_label: Their feet run to evil; therefore is judgment far from us
debates: Who speaks from the ninth verse onward
What peace they are said not to know
Whether a pronoun in the eighth verse should be singular or plural
outliers: Gill limits the confession to the few godly of the time, where Keil and Delitzsch have the prophet speaking for the nation as a whole
themes: Conduct described entirely in terms of roads
Peace withheld from those who make the paths crooked
Accusation answered by confession rather than defence
A guilt the better part of the nation cannot stand outside

10.pericope_label: We grope for the wall like the blind; our transgressions are multiplied
debates: Whether the tenth verse repeats a verb or has suffered a copying error
What the clause about desolate places means
Whether this confession is the model for the later ones or derived from them
outliers: Clarke emends a repeated verb on grounds of style alone, admitting the reading is older than every ancient version
themes: Blindness in full daylight
Grief expressed loudly and quietly at once
Penitence marked by the sound of its own verbs
Confession matching the indictment in severity

13.pericope_label: Truth is fallen in the street; he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey
debates: Whether the failure of judgment is God’s delay or human injustice
Whether the man who departs from evil is plundered, outlawed or thought mad
What it is that the Lord is said to have seen
outliers: Ellicott makes the Lord’s seeing refer to the people’s repentance rather than to their sins, against the first impression of the verse
themes: Personal confession widening into social diagnosis
Right pushed back as a boundary stone is moved
Integrity made dangerous to its owner
A rescue undertaken because no one else would

16.pericope_label: He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor
debates: Whether no man means no righteous man or no champion
Whether one word in the armour verse belongs to the text
What the two halves of the armour are severally for
outliers: Clarke argues a word of the seventeenth verse is an interpolation on five grounds, none of them manuscript evidence
themes: Grace enlarging in proportion to the sin
Complaint without the courage to act on it
A deliverer who has to be his own instrument
Armour divided between rescue and vengeance

18.pericope_label: When the enemy shall come in like a flood
debates: Whether the first half of the eighteenth verse is intelligible as it stands
Whether the enemy comes like a flood or the Lord comes like a rushing stream
Who lifts the standard, and what the standard-bearer does
outliers: Clarke corrects the eighteenth verse from an ancient paraphrase, holding the received Hebrew unintelligible
themes: Retribution measured by what was done
Judgment reaching the far-off lands as well as the near
A clause whose sense turns on one ambiguous noun
The Spirit pictured as striking the first blow

20.pericope_label: The Redeemer shall come to Zion; this is my covenant with them
debates: Whether the Redeemer comes to those who turn from transgression or turns transgression away
Whom the address about the Spirit and the words is spoken to
Which coming of the Redeemer is meant
outliers: Clarke traces the apostolic form of the quotation to two words read differently from the received Hebrew
themes: A promise closing an indictment
A covenant renewing the words spoken to Abram
Law inside the heart rather than outside the conscience
Doctrine promised to the third generation and beyond
